headline: Brunswick posts a strong quarter, raises full-year outlook
summary_short: Brunswick's Q2 2026 net sales rose 7.7% y/y to $1,557.8M with growth across all four segments, and GAAP diluted EPS (continuing operations) climbed 84.4% y/y to $1.66 as operating margin expanded 120bp to 8.3% on higher sales, favorable mix, and IEEPA tariff refunds.
summary_long: Second-quarter net sales rose 7.7% y/y to $1,557.8M, led by growth across all four segments — Propulsion +7.7%, Engine Parts & Accessories +8.9%, Navico Group +6.7%, Boat +4.6%. GAAP operating earnings rose 25.3% to $129.4M (8.3% margin, +120bp) on higher sales, favorable mix, and IEEPA tariff refunds; adjusted operating earnings were $150.1M (9.6% margin). Net earnings were $109.8M and diluted EPS $1.68, up from $0.89. Cash was $288.1M; long-term debt fell to $1,805.7M from $2,097.5M y/y. Brunswick raised full-year 2026 guidance: adjusted diluted EPS to $4.35-$4.75, net sales to $5.7B-$5.8B, and free cash flow to $400M or more, and set Q3 revenue guidance of $1.4B-$1.5B.

drivers.explanation: Sales grew across all four reporting segments for a fourth consecutive quarter, driven by steady OEM demand, healthy boating participation, favorable mix, and pricing actions taken in prior periods.
Higher sales, favorable mix, and operating execution, plus recognition of IEEPA tariff refunds, more than offset inflation, higher variable compensation, tariffs, and product-development investment.
Follows the operating-income gain, plus lower interest expense ($24.8M vs $30.0M y/y) and a tax benefit (effective rate -1.7% vs 20.8% y/y).
Driven by higher net income plus a modest reduction in weighted average diluted shares (65.5M vs 66.0M y/y).

Six-month operating cash flow of $251.5M was offset by $98.6M of capex, $57.2M of dividends, $31.2M of buybacks, and a $28.2M acquisition, and 2025's cash flow had included $267.6M of short-term debt proceeds not repeated in 2026.
Company reiterated a plan to retire at least $160 million of debt in 2026 to maintain an investment-grade balance sheet.

Fourth consecutive quarter of y/y sales growth across all segments; raised full-year 2026 guidance to adjusted diluted EPS of $4.35-$4.75, net sales of $5.7B-$5.8B, and free cash flow of $400M or more, citing IEEPA tariff refunds and strong operating execution.
